tasks.title: Retrieve Argentina-Washington correspondence, 1921-1925
tasks.collection: Embajada en Washington, Estados Unidos I (27.A)
tasks.research_gap: Underlying Argentine diplomatic records have not been examined. They may locate the origin of the Daumas/Dumont attribution and document what Argentina transmitted to Washington.
tasks.critical_rule: Preserve Daumas, Dumont, or any other attribution exactly as written; distinguish Argentine-authored records from enclosures or copied U.S. statements.
tasks.high_value_result: A dated Argentine-origin record identifying the sculptor, original work, fabrication or copy process, donor, or information formally transmitted to the U.S. government.
inheritance_questions: Is the statement authored by the Argentine record creator or enclosed/copied from another source?
Does the wording identify an upstream document?
Can the Daumas/Dumont conflict be dated earlier than the current sources?

tasks.title: Retrieve Revista Legado No. 3 San Martin source trail
tasks.repository: Archivo General de la Nacion, Argentina / libraries holding Revista Legado
tasks.collection: Revista Legado, Publicacion Digital No. 3, August 2016; Nicolas Gutierrez material cited by Instituto Nacional Sanmartiniano
tasks.research_gap: The Instituto explicitly identifies Revista Legado No. 3 as the source behind its list of foreign copies, including Washington. The article and its own citations have not been ingested.
priority_units: Pages identifying Washington as a copy
Footnotes, bibliography, archival call numbers and image captions supporting the Washington statement
tasks.critical_rule: Treat the 2016 article as downstream research until its cited archival roots are identified; do not count the Instituto republication and Revista Legado as independent lineages.
tasks.high_value_result: The complete article plus the exact upstream archival or bibliographic source used for the Washington-copy statement.
inheritance_questions: What exact source supports the Washington-copy statement?
Does Revista Legado cite archival evidence or another secondary work?
Does the Instituto page reproduce Revista Legado rather than independently research the claim?

tasks.title: Retrieve Uruguay-Washington Artigas correspondence, 1947-1951
tasks.repository: Archivo Historico-Diplomatico, Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, Uruguay
tasks.collection: Sub Fondo Legaciones y Embajadas, 2.10 Embajada de la Republica en Estados Unidos (1900-1990)
tasks.research_gap: Underlying 1947-1951 diplomatic correspondence may establish donor language, fabrication, casting, shipment, installation, dedication, and the relationship between the Washington bronze and San Jose de Mayo.
priority_units: Folders concerning Artigas, Washington, shipment, casting or dedication
Enclosures captured separately from covering correspondence
tasks.critical_rule: Separate fabrication/casting from authorship/model lineage; preserve enclosures and cited upstream sources as distinct records.
tasks.high_value_result: A contemporaneous Uruguayan record identifying who authorized, fabricated, cast, shipped, presented, or described the Washington statue and its relationship to San Jose de Mayo.

epistemic_targets.proposition: Identity of the Washington Artigas caster/foundry

inheritance_questions: Is a statement original to the diplomatic record or copied from an enclosure?
Does the record identify a foundry, procurement file, shipment record or press source?
Can Smithsonian's Montevideo/early-1940s metadata be traced to an earlier root?

tasks.title: Retrieve the 21 Aug 1949 El Dia Artigas article
tasks.repository: Anaforas / Universidad de la Republica and Biblioteca Nacional de Uruguay ecosystem
tasks.collection: Suplemento Dominical de El Dia, 21 Aug 1949
tasks.research_gap: Indexes identify a pre-dedication article titled 'Monumento a Artigas en Washington', but the pages have not been retrieved.
priority_units: Adjacent source or credit lines revealing publicity or wire-copy origin
tasks.critical_rule: The index proves only existence. Classify the retrieved article as original reporting, official/diplomatic publicity, wire copy, editorial, or unknown.
tasks.high_value_result: A complete scan with metadata and text/images bearing on production, financing, shipment, installation, or donor narrative.
inheritance_questions: Is the article original reporting, an official release, wire copy or unattributed reproduction?
Does it name a source for fabrication/casting statements?
Do photographs or captions supply independent observable evidence?

tasks.title: Retrieve the 1894 Blanes commission and 1896 Dante Costa contract
tasks.repository: Uruguay government archives / Diario Oficial / relevant San Jose administrative archive
tasks.collection: Records underlying the historical findings reproduced in Resolution 732/004
tasks.research_gap: Resolution 732/004 identifies the 14 Nov 1894 commission and 25 Jul 1896 Costa contract, but the underlying records are not represented.
priority_units: Attached specifications identifying model, plaster, casting, dimensions, payment, supervision or destination
tasks.critical_rule: Retrieve the underlying act or contract, not another later summary. Distinguish commission/authorship, model execution, plaster work and bronze casting.
tasks.high_value_result: Images or authoritative reproductions of the original 1894 and 1896 records with identifiers and complete relevant clauses.
inheritance_questions: Does Resolution 732/004 accurately reproduce the original act/contract?
Do the originals cite prior decisions, sketches or specifications?
Which propositions are explicit contract terms versus later historical interpretation?

tasks.title: Retrieve the U.S. diplomatic spine for the Cuban Friendship Urn, 1926-1928
tasks.repository: National Archives and Records Administration, United States
tasks.collection: RG 59, 1910-29 Central Decimal File; USS Maine memorial in Cuba
tasks.research_gap: The preserved U.S. diplomatic spine needs reconstruction and comparison with independently recoverable Cuban contemporary records.
priority_units: Surrounding 1926-1928 correspondence on fabrication, transfer, custody, ceremony and material lineage
tasks.critical_rule: Separate ceremony/presentation, donor identity, object identity, and material provenance. Missing Cuban records are ARCHIVAL_GAP, not negative evidence.
tasks.high_value_result: Contemporaneous records separately establishing transfer, object identity, donor/presenter language, and material reuse claims.
inheritance_questions: Who originated each donor/presentation/material statement?
Is a diplomatic dispatch reporting direct knowledge, quoting Cuban officials, or transmitting an enclosure?
Can later NPS wording be traced to this file?

tasks.title: Recover an independent Cuban contemporary record lane for the Friendship Urn
tasks.repository: Multiple Cuban and international digitized repositories
tasks.collection: Cuban newspapers, official publications, presidential/diplomatic texts, conference materials and historical photographs, 1926-1928
tasks.research_gap: A Cuban-origin contemporary lane is needed to test the U.S. diplomatic account without assuming a complete mirror archive survives.
priority_units: Historical images documenting memorial, fragments, urn, inscription or ceremony
tasks.critical_rule: Classify published records by origin: original reporting, official-text reproduction, diplomatic release, wire copy, editorial, or unknown. Reproductions of one upstream statement remain one lineage.
tasks.high_value_result: A Cuban-origin contemporary source that independently confirms, contradicts, qualifies, or more precisely describes fabrication, material origin, donor identity, presentation, or custody.
inheritance_questions: Is the item original Cuban reporting or reproduction of a U.S./official statement?
Does it identify a named Cuban official, workshop or documentary source?
Are multiple newspapers reproducing one wire or government release?

tasks.title: Retrieve the 1929 Public Buildings and Public Parks report and RG 42 installation records
tasks.repository: U.S. Government publication holdings and National Archives, RG 42
tasks.collection: Annual Report of the Director of Public Buildings and Public Parks, FY1929 (SuDoc PB 1.1:929), p. 64; related RG 42 records
tasks.research_gap: Later NPS documentation cites the 1929 annual report for the urn, but the underlying page and associated operational records have not been inspected.
priority_units: Related work orders, correspondence, photographs, site plans, receipt, installation or custody records
tasks.critical_rule: Do not infer p. 64 from the later NPS citation. Separate receipt, installation, dedication, custody, presentation and material provenance.
tasks.high_value_result: The cited page and related contemporary administrative records documenting what the park agency received, installed, recorded or knew in 1928-1929.

epistemic_targets.proposition: 1928-1929 federal receipt and installation of the Cuban Friendship Urn

inheritance_questions: What exactly does p. 64 say rather than what later NPS sources say it says?
Do later NPS narratives reproduce the annual report?
Do RG 42 records add independent operational knowledge or merely repeat diplomatic paperwork?
